column2: Capture system activity, manufacturing artifacts, runtime telemetry, and analyst-facing evidence for investigation and research.

Core logging/analysis architecture plus relevant supporting evidence components: System & Access Logs, G-code & File Artifacts, Runtime Telemetry, Analyst Tools, Alert Engine, Session Timeline, Evidence Store, and Artifact Hashing.
3D Printer Physical Simulator → Logging, Storage and Analyst Support → Telemetry & Analysis

column4: Implementation Approach: existing software, extend existing, or build new?

column3: I mapped System & Access Logs to Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels because authentication, API, and session activity are operational events that must be captured through the printer environment's logging path.
column4: Build custom HoneyPrint event capture while reusing web-server, API, and session metadata where available. (Python (aiohttp middleware + logging + datetime + structlog))
column5: Record authentication attempts, API activity, sessions, and management-surface interactions in a consistent evidence stream.
column6: Timestamped access/session events with actor, endpoint/action, result, and relevant context for later correlation.

column2: Stage 2 > Hardware > Job-package storage; Stage 2 > Network > Transfer to printer network
column3: I mapped G-code & File Artifacts to Stage 2 > Hardware > Job-package storage and Stage 2 > Network > Transfer to printer network because these artifacts are retained as build-job files and originate from upload or transfer operations into the printer workflow.
column4: Extend HoneyPrint file handling with persistent artifact storage and metadata; reuse normal filesystem primitives and hashing. (Python (pathlib + aiofiles + hashlib + mimetypes))
column5: Preserve uploaded or generated G-code/configuration artifacts so attacker-supplied manufacturing content can be reviewed later.
column6: Stored files plus metadata such as filename, size, timestamps, hash, source/session, and execution linkage.

column2: Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics; Stage 3 > Hardware > Cameras, thermal & process sensors; Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels
column3: I mapped Runtime Telemetry to Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics, Stage 3 > Hardware > Cameras, thermal & process sensors, and Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels because it combines live machine-state analysis, sensor readings, and captured runtime events.
column4: Build/extend a shared HoneyPrint telemetry pipeline tied to simulated printer state and sensor models; persist selected events when needed. (Python (asyncio.Queue + dataclasses + json + motor))
column5: Capture changing printer state, sensor values, commands, faults, and simulator events while the honeypot is running.
column6: Time-ordered telemetry for motion, extrusion, temperature, power/fault state, print-job state, sensors, and significant events.

column2: Stage 5 > Software > MES / PLM feedback systems; Stage 5 > Network > Reporting / API exchange
column3: I mapped Analyst Tools to Stage 5 > Software > MES / PLM feedback systems and Stage 5 > Network > Reporting / API exchange because the search and visualization layer turns captured evidence into analyst-facing results that can be reported or fed back to higher-level systems.
column4: Build/extend the custom HoneyPrint analyst API/dashboard and reuse standard querying/visualization libraries where useful. (Python (aiohttp + aiohttp-jinja2 + Jinja2 + motor + pandas))
column5: Let researchers search, filter, summarize, and visualize captured sessions, alerts, files, commands, and telemetry.
column6: Analyst-facing views and query results that connect raw evidence to sessions, alerts, artifacts, and state changes.

column2: Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics; Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels
column3: I mapped Alert Engine to Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics and Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels because it evaluates runtime anomalies and faults and then records the resulting alerts as monitored operational events.
column4: Build/extend HoneyPrint alert generation over normalized risk, fault, and activity events. (Python (dataclasses + enum + motor + datetime))
column5: Turn selected suspicious commands, state changes, and fault conditions into analyst-visible alerts.
column6: Structured alerts linked to sessions, commands, artifacts, and relevant printer state.

column2: Stage 4 > Software > Traceability / process logging; Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels
column3: I mapped Session Timeline to Stage 4 > Software > Traceability / process logging and Stage 3 > Network > Monitoring & logging channels because it reconstructs ordered activity from captured events to provide traceable interaction history.
column4: Extend event correlation with stable session IDs and sequence/timestamp fields. (Python (uuid + itertools.count + time.monotonic + datetime))
column5: Reconstruct the ordered sequence of access, file, command, telemetry, and fault activity across interfaces.
column6: Per-session chronological timelines connecting adversary actions to simulator consequences.

column2: Stage 5 > Network > QC data upload / database
column3: I mapped Evidence Store to Stage 5 > Network > QC data upload / database because it persistently stores collected HoneyPrint evidence in a database for later querying and analysis.
column4: Reuse MongoDB with local JSON/JSONL fallback and custom HoneyPrint failover logic. (Python (motor/pymongo + aiofiles + json + tenacity))
column5: Persist captured evidence even when the primary database is unavailable.
column6: Durable structured records in MongoDB or local fallback storage for later analyst queries.

column2: Stage 5 > Software > Quality & certification software; Stage 5 > Network > QC data upload / database
column3: I mapped Artifact Hashing to Stage 5 > Software > Quality & certification software and Stage 5 > Network > QC data upload / database because SHA-256 provides file-integrity verification and the resulting hash metadata is stored with the evidence records.
column4: Reuse SHA-256 hashing and extend the HoneyPrint artifact metadata schema. (Python (hashlib + aiofiles + motor))
column5: Uniquely identify uploaded or generated files and detect repeated or modified artifacts across sessions.
column6: Cryptographic hashes stored with artifact metadata and linked to uploads, sessions, and execution records.
